## Pull request overview

This PR completes P2 (Advanced Views & Features) and P3 (Mobile Testing & QA) from the roadmap, advancing protocol alignment from ~55% to ~85%. The implementation adds five new protocol bridge modules that transform `@objectstack/spec` schemas into runtime-usable configurations, enhances the DashboardRenderer with header support, and establishes comprehensive mobile testing infrastructure.

**Changes:**
- Five protocol bridge modules (DndProtocol, KeyboardProtocol, NotificationProtocol, ResponsiveProtocol, SharingProtocol) with transformation functions for spec schemas
- Type re-exports for P2.3/P2.4 schemas (SharingConfig, EmbedConfig, AddRecordConfig, AppearanceConfig, UserActionsConfig, ViewTab)
- DashboardRenderer header rendering with title, description, action buttons, recordCount badge, and userActions config
- Mobile testing suite: visual regression, touch interaction, keyboard, performance, and accessibility tests
- Storybook mobile viewport presets (iPhone SE, iPhone 14, iPad Mini, Pixel 5)

### Reviewed changes

Copilot reviewed 24 out of 24 changed files in this pull request and generated 7 comments.

Test name says "swipe gesture on navigation sidebar" but the test only performs a simple tap at the center of the viewport and verifies the body is visible. This doesn't actually test any swipe gesture functionality. Consider either implementing actual swipe gesture testing (e.g., using touchscreen.swipe() or a sequence of touchstart/touchmove/touchend events) or renaming the test to accurately reflect what it does (e.g., "touch interaction works on mobile viewport").

The interaction response time test uses force click which may not accurately measure real user interaction latency. The `force: true` option bypasses actionability checks (like visibility and stability), which could mask actual responsiveness issues. Consider removing the force option to measure realistic user interaction latency, or add a comment explaining why forced clicking is necessary for this performance benchmark.
```suggestion
      await buttons.first().click();
```

The `frameborder` attribute is deprecated in HTML5. Modern browsers ignore this attribute and it's recommended to use CSS `border: none` in the style attribute instead. Since the code already includes `border: none` in the style attribute (lines 123, 125), the frameborder attribute is redundant and can be safely removed.
```suggestion

```

These accessibility tests verify plain HTML elements (button, form, nav, dialog, table) rather than actual ObjectUI components from @object-ui/components. While these tests confirm that axe-core works correctly at mobile viewport widths, they don't test the accessibility of the actual ObjectUI component library. Consider adding tests for ObjectUI components like Button, Input, Card, Dialog from `@object-ui/components` to ensure the actual components meet WCAG 2.1 AA standards at mobile viewports.

Unnecessary React import. Since this file uses JSX, React 17+ automatically transforms JSX without requiring an explicit React import. The import on line 20 can be removed to align with modern React conventions.
```suggestion

```

Touch target size validation logic is inconsistent with the existing mobile-viewport.spec.ts. This test uses AND logic (both width AND height >= 32px), while mobile-viewport.spec.ts uses OR logic (either width OR height >= 32px). This discrepancy could lead to different test results for the same UI elements. Consider aligning both tests to use the same logic - the OR approach is more lenient and practical for real-world scenarios where some buttons may be wide but short (or vice versa).
```suggestion
          if (box.width >= MINIMUM_TOUCH_TARGET_PX || box.height >= MINIMUM_TOUCH_TARGET_PX) {
```
